messages:
Samir: Hey team — customer  acme-corp is seeing a ~3x delta between their dashboard embed counts and the invoice for last week. They say they only sent ~120k inputs but invoice shows 360k embed units. Any ideas?
Priya: Yikes. Did they use pairwise/rerank or regular embeddings?
Samir: They used embeddings for indexing + a rerank endpoint for similarity. Billing lines are labeled 'embeddings' not 'rerank' though.
Marta: Can you grab their request logs (raw requests + status codes)? Pairwise can multiply counts if mis-accounted.
Samir: Uploaded here: https://redwood.internal/support/reqs/ACME-4387 — request body shows batches of 50, but I see some 0-length inputs occasionally due to upstream cleanup.
Jules: Quick thought: we had a meter change in oct where padded inputs from the batching pipeline were supposed to be excluded, but a fallback path might still count them. @BillingBot any hits?
BillingBot: Found matching invoice lines. Metering service logged entries for 360,000 vector records for acme-corp between 2026-02-10 and 2026-02-16. Many entries show source="embed-pipeline" and reason="counted".
Priya: Can you paste the exact request snippet? Even one sample will help.
Samir: Sure — sample from logs:
```json
{"model":"rwd-embed-64k-v1","inputs":["doc1","doc2","","doc4"],"batch_size":50,"pairwise":false}
```
Marta: Aha — there's an empty string in inputs. Our batching/padding code treats "" as a valid input when generating padding vectors, then the metering layer later de-duplicates only by payload hash which misses blank entries due to normalization mismatch.
Jules: So in retries the pipeline re-enqueues a padded placeholder with id=null and the metering layer counts it again. That matches a 3x multiplier if some requests were retried twice.
Samir: Customer says they had intermittent 500s during ingestion that triggered a client retry loop. So retried requests + padding could explain the delta.
Priya: We should repro locally. Steps: 1) craft batch of 50 with a few empty strings 2) simulate transient 500 from runtime 3) client retries with same body 4) observe metering logs.
Marta: I ran a quick repro — confirmed meter_entries increased by number_of_inputs * (1 + retries). Patch idea: meter should ignore inputs that are empty/zero-length after normalization and the dedupe key should include the normalized input hash + idempotency-key if present.
Jules: Can we hotfix to avoid immediate double charges? Maybe retroactively mark recent meter entries with source="embed-pipeline" + input_len=0 as nonbillable, but need finance sign-off.
Samir: Logged a billing escalation: #ACME-4387-INV-ADJ and pinged finance. Customer asked for short-term mitigation — suggested they set idempotency-key header on retries. They agreed to change client today.
BillingBot: Created ticket FIN-2026-78 for possible adjustment.
eng-oncall: Patch PR ready: https://redwood.internal/pull/9876 — removes empty inputs earlier in the pipeline and adds normalized-hash dedupe. CI passing. Will ship to canary in 2 hours.
Marta: Also adding a migration script to tag recent meter rows where input_norm_len=0 and source="embed-pipeline" for manual review.
Priya: Good. Post-deploy, let's monitor metrics: meter.rate(acme-corp), invoice-preview, and error-rate for embed service. If client still sees delta after idempotency-key change and patch, we'll consider an invoice credit.
Samir: Noted. I'll update the customer and keep thread posted. Thanks all :pray:
Jules: Follow-up: add a validation on client libs to filter out empty strings before sending. Sending lib patch to sdk team.
Samir: Closing loop later today after canary verification.
